abstract: Secondary active transporters use the thermodynamically favorable movement of an ion down its electrochemical gradient to drive substrate accumulation against a concentration gradient. For the human serotonin transporter (SERT), strict coupling between Na and 5-HT transport is essential for maintaining neurotransmitter homeostasis, yet the structural mechanism by which Na binding enforces this coupling is incompletely understood. Here, we identify an interaction network through which Na coordination at the cation site Ct2 (also known as Na2) modulates conformational change on both sides of the transporter. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that Na occupancy of Ct2 stabilizes specific interactions between residues in TM5, TM8, and TM1 that together gate aqueous access to the cytoplasmic and extracellular pathways. Disruption of this network through mutations at Ct2 residues Asp437 and Ser438, or at the TM5 residue Thr284, reduces the concentrative power of SERT and allows a constitutive Na conductance, consistent with uncoupled Na uniport. These findings reveal how structural integrity at and around the Ct2 site enforces obligatory Na-5-HT coupling and thereby sustains the thermodynamic efficiency of serotonin uptake.
